EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong pair of low-frequency bands at 739 and 594 cm⁻¹, characteristic of organochloride C–Cl stretching modes; the presence of two such bands with one very intense (739) is especially consistent with a gem-dichloro group. The clear amide I band at 1639 cm⁻¹ matches a tertiary amide C=O, and the CH stretches at 2937 cm⁻¹ (plus a weaker band at 2821 cm⁻¹ likely due to CH overtones/Fermi resonance) and CH₃ deformation bands at 1458/1416 cm⁻¹ fit an N,N-dimethylamide (supported by GFQ-003 for C–H stretching/bending). Additional bands at 961 and 1015 cm⁻¹ align with CH₃ rocking and C–N/C–C skeletal modes of a dimethylamide. Among candidates, CCC(Cl)(Cl)C(=O)N(C)C uniquely explains the gem-dichloro signatures together with a tertiary amide.
